steps.text: Oven to 220 °C fan with a baking tray inside to heat.
Chicken (85/110 g) between two sheets of paper, bashed to an even 1 cm. Salt both sides. Beaten egg (25 g) in one bowl, seasoned panko (20/25 g) in another. Egg, then panko, pressed on firmly.
Onto the HOT tray, 3 g of the rapeseed oil brushed over the crumb. 18 minutes, turned once at 10.

Sauce: onion (40/50 g) and carrot (60/70 g) diced small, into a pan with the remaining 3/5 g rapeseed oil, medium, 6 minutes until soft. 1½ tsp curry powder, ½ tsp garam masala and a pinch of sugar (1 g) — 60 seconds more.
Blitz the sauce smooth with a stick blender. It should coat the back of a spoon — loosen with a splash of water if it's gone too far.
Rice and cauliflower (30/42 g dry + 130/160 g) warmed.
Broccoli (140/165 g) steamed 4 minutes, still squeaky.
Chicken out, rested a minute, sliced across. Sauce poured BESIDE it, not over.

why: The preheated tray is what replaces the deep fryer — the underside starts cooking on contact instead of sitting in its own steam. And blitzing the carrot and onion is what thickens the sauce; there is no flour anywhere in this.
notes: D0-003: the whole 6/8 g table total is oil that hits either the sauce pan (step 4, 3 g) or the hot roasting tray (step 3, remainder 3/5 g) — no raw dressing use anywhere in this dish, so it becomes rapeseed_oil in full, restated across the two steps (3+3=6 her, 3+5=8 him).

Cross-file id conflict resolved: _ingredients.A.json originally defined its own 'sugar' record (freebie:true, matching this card's trace 'pinch of sugar'). _ingredients.B.json (Week B rewriter, parallel) independently defines 'sugar' too, for an explicit 1 tsp in a B dish, freebie:false. Rather than ship two conflicting per100g/freebie records under the same id (fails L9), this file now weighs the pinch as 1/1 g in covers using B's canonical sugar record (400 kcal/100 g) instead of listing it as a freebie. Drift is nil (well under 1 kcal at 1 g).
